correctness.rationale: The code definition is exact and open-neighborhood based. Necessity: selected subgraph is induced 1-regular, forcing row/column-disjoint edges; an empty row/column collides with a selected mate whenever a corresponding oriented edge is present, and at most one empty line in either orientation. Sufficiency: all allowed configurations have four disjoint horizontal/vertical signature profiles in the mixed case and two by cardinality in pure cases, each uniquely reconstructing the cell; selected singleton signatures are all distinct. Factorials count labeled block assignments with all symmetries removed. The standalone verifier independently checked every even-size subset in twelve small boards and explicit large constructions; it is supporting finite evidence, not an infinite proof.

evidence: Cappelle et al., arXiv:2103.07972v4, Theorem 2.2 states a general necessary two-neighbor condition but not a sufficient one for graphs of arbitrary girth; Sections 3–4 classify P4-tidy graphs and complementary prisms of cographs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The broad necessary OLD_oind condition does not give signature separation for rook graphs: the new proof checks it explicitly by four row-column profiles. Closed-neighborhood locating parameters, or stronger self/solid criteria on different products, neither identify nor enumerate all induced-1-regular open-locating codes. Thus none of these inspected broader results entails the exact arithmetic existence or labeled counts.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The final claim has three nontrivial parts: necessary-and-sufficient exact parameter families, rigidity that all admissible sets are of one size, and factorial counts of *all* labeled admissible sets. General necessary bounds and distinct-code minimum formulas do not imply any of those jointly. The scientific comparison was made by statement implication rather than title similarity; remaining unindexed-literature risk is acknowledged.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalent language includes identifying open codes subject to open-independence, and induced-paired sets with the stronger requirement that all open-neighborhood signatures be nonempty and distinct. Generic induced matching or paired domination does not enforce the locating condition, and ordinary or closed-neighborhood codes are different. No exact equivalent classification for L(K_{m,n}) or rook graphs was identified; failure to find one alone is not evidence of novelty.

value.rationale: This solves the entire natural two-factor Cartesian complete-graph family for an identification parameter with a rigid induced 1-regular sensor constraint. The sharp arithmetic feasibility conditions exclude almost all rectangle dimensions, characterize every feasible set, and determine exact labeled multiplicity and optimal size. The 3-divisibility condition on square side length is structurally motivated, not an arbitrarily selected slice or a small numerical increment.
